note.note:
Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male with 3–6 months of low mood, fatigue, reduced appetite, ~1-stone unintentional weight loss, and situational palpitations → initial impression of depressive symptoms and/or relapse of hypothyroidism; blood work arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Loss of appetite and energy for ≈3.5 months; feels “down,” wife notes decreased libido.  
• Weight loss: ~1 stone over ≈6 months.  
• Associated symptoms: Occasional nausea (no vomiting), headaches, episodic palpitations + feeling “can’t breathe” in elevators; no chest pain; can walk a mile without dyspnoea (has been sedentary lately). Bowels normal; no diarrhoea, bleeding, or mucus. No reflux.  
• Pertinent negatives: No persistent exertional SOB, no vomiting, no chest pain, no bowel change or bleeding.  
• Past medical history: Primary hypothyroidism; stopped levothyroxine several months ago after changing doctors. No recent blood tests.  
• Allergies: Not discussed.  
• Medications: None currently (levothyroxine stopped).  
• Social / preventive: Lawyer; job change 3.5 months ago. No other social history elicited (tobacco, alcohol, drugs, exercise). No preventive care discussed.

Examination:
Tele-consultation – no vitals or physical exam performed.

Impression:
1. Low mood / possible Major Depressive Disorder – low mood, anhedonia, appetite and weight loss, fatigue.  
2. Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism – history of underactive thyroid, stopped replacement; can cause fatigue and mood changes.  
3. Anaemia or other metabolic cause – fatigue, headaches; to be ruled out with bloods.  
Situational palpitations may represent panic episodes; organic arrhythmia considered less likely given normal exertional tolerance.

Plan:
• Order routine labs: CBC, renal profile, liver profile, thyroid function tests, vitamin B12/folate, iron studies, glucose ± HbA1c.  
• Patient to phone support number (in app) to arrange blood draw; clinician to submit lab requisition.  
• Follow-up: Patient will receive text when results ready → book follow-up appointment.  
• Safety-netting: Attend A&E or re-contact service for any chest pain, sustained palpitations, vomiting, or change in bowel habits.  
• Consider physical examination and further cardiac evaluation if bloods unremarkable yet palpitations persist.  
• Mental health assessment and support to be considered at follow-up depending on results/symptom progression.

Quality checks
● Missing expected elements: allergies, current medication list confirmation, family history, smoking/alcohol/drug use, vitals, mental-health screening (PHQ-9/GAD-7), sleep pattern, occupational stress details, follow-up timeframe.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: Adequate history of present illness; limited social history and no physical exam or vitals possible in tele-visit.
